feed.title: antxiko — commented disassemblies of 8-bit games
feed.subtitle: Old 8-bit binaries taken apart byte by byte and commented, with the tools to rebuild them: nothing gets claimed that the binary does not show, and the source has to give the original back, byte for byte. Right now that means 75 MSX games.

entry.title: Metal Gear 2: everything animated, played by the cartridge
entry.summary: The eleven boss fights in order of appearance, 22 different enemies, Snake's moves and the radar, all as GIFs played by the cartridge at the MSX's own pace (one game frame every 5 of the VDP, measured in openMSX); the whole intro and ending in one GIF each; every weapon and item with its drawing; the transceiver conversations side by side with their translation; the two eggs, a boa and an owl. Fixed: broken boss sprites and a noisy radar, both faults of the emulator.

entry.title: Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1990 Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake for MSX2, its 512 KB 100% explained and commented to 45.9%. The 20 zones with their 274 rooms and 57 special rooms, Snake, the enemies, the eleven boss fights, the weapons, the equipment, the radar and the sequences painted by the cartridge itself and checked against openMSX; every transceiver conversation, the texts, 44 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine and the debug monitor hidden in the last bank.

entry.title: What Konami's cartridges share, routine by routine
entry.summary: The 58 Konami disassemblies in the series compared with each other instruction by instruction, with the addresses set aside: 1,252 of the 1,653 pairs share at least one block of code. The games' code pages now list the cartridges each one shares the most with, and the whole matrix is on The routines, in the series database. Nemesis 2 and Salamander lead with 210 blocks; Pro Yakyuu and Pennant Race 2 share 119.

entry.title: Gekitotsu Pennant Race 2, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1989 Gekitotsu Pennant Race 2 for MSX2, 100% explained and commented to 40.4%. The screens, both stadiums whole, the pitching screen, the batter's swing, the play signs and the team sheet drawn from the ROM with the cartridge's own routines, the six teams with every player and how the ERA is worked out, the texts, the SELECT trick and 17 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine; all checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi, in English
entry.summary: The tutorial patch is now a full English translation: menus, rules, rivals, call menus, yaku and scores, the call-outs, the title logo (TILE MAGICIAN), the attract introduction with MAHJONG over the jigsaw, and digits and E S W N on the tiles in their four sizes. The tutorial is still on F1.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi tutorial, now with the tiles
entry.summary: Text alone did not teach anyone mahjong. The tutorial is now nine screens drawn with the game's own tiles, letters and kanji: the suits, winds and dragons, the goal, the sets, the calls, riichi and tsumo, and each menu entry beside its kanji.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi tutorial patch: see it running
entry.summary: The patch's page now opens with an animation of the tutorial, taken from the patched cartridge in openMSX: the menu, F1, the five pages and back to the menu.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi: the music, all 48 yaku measured, and what a game reads
entry.summary: Fourteen PSG tunes and effects played by the cartridge's own engine (the title tune checked against openMSX frame by frame), with F1-F5 choosing the background music; every yaku code now seen coming out of the game; and fifteen minutes of play with a watchpoint on every ROM read.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi gets a tutorial in English
entry.summary: An IPS patch: F1 on the first menu opens five pages that explain how to play, the two menus, the calls, the rivals and the music keys. Everything else in the game is unchanged.

entry.title: Hai no Majutsushi - Mahjong 2, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1989 Japanese mahjong for MSX2, 100% explained and commented to 25.9%. The screens in order, the eight characters and the seven counters that give each its style (and drift with the hands you win), the ten rules, the yaku measured by running the game's own code, and the eight digital voices decoded from the ROM.

entry.title: King Kong 2: ROCKMAN and STONEMAN never head for Mitchel at random
entry.summary: A comparison that can never be met: the branch that aims at Mitchel is never taken from the random choice. Proved by the code itself.

entry.title: Knightmare: frame 0x0B never gets the row adjustment
entry.summary: A mask that leaves 0, 4, 8 or 12 compared with 11: it can never be equal. Proved from the code; which frames appear in a game is not measured.

entry.title: Hinotori: a comparison for Gao that can never match
entry.summary: It makes no difference to the game, because both paths lead to the same place; noted on the findings page.

entry.title: Game Master 2: the 24-bit subtraction lowers the wrong byte
entry.summary: The biorhythm's subtraction routine, on a borrow, lowers the fourth byte instead of the third. Measured by running the routine.

entry.title: Nemesis 3: two comparisons that cannot be met
entry.summary: Boss 4's limit ends up at 0xE8 instead of 0xF8, and one enemy never tells the lower half of the screen apart. Logical proofs from the code.

entry.title: Nemesis 2: two checks that cannot be met
entry.summary: Boss 2 goes down to 0x80 instead of 0x68, and the right-edge clipping never runs. Logical proofs from the code; the effect on screen is not measured.

entry.title: Super Cobra: the terrain's shot ignores the row
entry.summary: The carry of one comparison is lost before it is used, so every terrain shot in class 0 zones aims at the ship. Logical proof; effect in a game not measured.

entry.title: Metal Gear: two bugs in the game, measured
entry.summary: Two bugs found by Manuel Pazos, now confirmed by running the cartridge's own routines: the weapon and equipment windows leave gaps when two slots in a row are empty, and only the slow guards ever drop a ration or ammo. Thanks to Néstor for bringing them in.

entry.title: Nemesis 3: The Eve of Destruction, taken apart
entry.summary: Konami's 1988 Nemesis 3 for MSX, 100% explained and commented to 41.3%. The eleven stages with every route drawn from the ROM, the secret entrances and the three maps that open stages 10 and 11, the four ships with every weapon firing, the enemies, the bosses, the story and the ending animated, the pause passwords and 26 PSG and SCC tunes from its own engine; all checked against openMSX.

entry.title: Contra: the enemies of each stage, and the route through each base
entry.summary: The enemy sheet is now one row per stage, every figure with its stage's palette (none caught in the fade-in) and lined up in equal cells. And each 3D base now shows the route from the entrance to the core: the door to take in every room and where the other one leads.
